rubrics.justification: It correctly recognizes a very poor-quality early blastocyst with absent/degenerate ICM and TE, but it misstates the expansion criterion for Gardner 1 as less than half rather than at least half the embryo volume, and it adds speculative details such as apoptotic bodies/debris not clearly discernible.

It integrates age, ovarian reserve, tubal factor diagnosis, sperm parameters, endometrium, and first-cycle status well, highlighting the discordance between favorable patient factors and poor embryo morphology, though it could better acknowledge that even good-prognosis patients can produce occasional poor embryos.

The reasoning is structured and internally consistent overall, with conclusions largely following from the poor morphology, but it overstates certainty by calling the embryo essentially non-viable and assigning near-zero chance based on morphology alone.

It is broadly aligned in recognizing 1DD as very poor prognosis, but the incorrect definition of expansion grade 1 and the strong recommendation against transfer/near-zero viability are more absolute than typical evidence-based counseling; routine strong endorsement of PGT-A in a 33-year-old good-prognosis first cycle is also not fully guideline-driven.

It provides clear next steps including counseling, review of the full embryology report, and future-cycle planning, but some recommendations are overly one-sided and do not sufficiently discuss individualized/shared decision-making if this were the only embryo available.
